To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of polyelectrolytes and PEG-containing copolymers is an effective strategy for the reduction of nonspecific cell adhesion to PDMS.

the combination of PDADMAC and PAA or PAH and PAA as PEMs can effectively reduce the initial cell attachment and the adhesion strength to the channel walls of S. cerevesiae DSM 2156 in PDMS microfluidic devices, and that the adsorption of PEG-based copolymer PAA-g-PEO onto the PEMs further reduces the initial cell attachment as well as the adhesion strength by at least one order of magnitude.
the combination of PEMs and PEGylation of PDMS surfaces can reduce yeast cell adhesion to PDMS microfluidic devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel surface functionalization methods for PDMS-based microdevices.
the development of novel functionalized PDMS surfaces for microfluidic devices, and the PEMs are considered as a promising approach to achieve a long-term stable cell adhesion reduction.
the development of a novel approach for the functionalization of microfluidic devices based on PDMS with the potential to promote plankton growth of S. cereviase inside such systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PEMs are a promising tool to reduce nonspecific cell adhesion in PDMS-based microsystems.
the PEMs and PAA-g-PEGS are promising tools to reduce the cell attachment strength in microfluidic PDMS devices.
PEMs are suitable to reduce yeast adhesion in PDMS microfluidic devices, whereas PAA-g-PEO is suitable to reduce the initial attachment of yeast cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PEMs are promising for reducing cell adhesion to microfluidic devices.

a suitable PEM modification effectively reduces yeast cell adhesion to PDMS surfaces and the further reduction in cell adhesion strength can be achieved by grafting PAA-g-PEC copolymers onto the PEMs.
PEMs are promising tools for the reduction of cell adhesion strength in PDMS-based microchannels, which is a prerequisite for the development of a fully functionalized PDMS-based microsystem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PEMs and the graft copolymer are promising candidates for surface modification of microfluidic devices for applications in cell culture and cell-based assays.
the combination of a suitable PEM and PAA-g-PEO copolymer is an effective strategy for reducing yeast cell adhesion on PDMS surfaces in a microfluidic device.
the combination of a PEM and a PEGylated copolymer can be used to control cell adhesion strength and thus to improve cell culture inside microfluidic devices.
